background_notes.fact: If d is an extended nonnegative real, delta is a finite nonnegative real and d<=ofReal(delta), then d is finite, 0<=d.toReal<=delta and ofReal(d.toReal)=d. For finite nonnegative reals a,b, ofReal(a)<=ofReal(b) is equivalent to a<=b.

grounds.reason: L1 gives delta>0 and L2 bounds each d=ediam(V_i) by ofReal(delta).
D003 identifies finite extended nonnegative values with their real values.

background_notes.justification: The finite bound excludes the top element. The order-preserving identification of the finite nonnegative part with the nonnegative real half-line gives the two inequalities and inverse conversion. This also permits passing from a pointwise edist bound to the real absolute-distance bound used in S002.

background_notes.fact: The real numbers with their usual order and metric bornology form an order bornology: metric-bounded sets are order-bounded, and every interval with finite real endpoints is metric-bounded. Thus the real structure satisfies the structural order/bornology premise of M018.

grounds.reason: M018 requires a conditionally complete lattice with compatible bornology.
Each Bproj_i is contained in a finite interval in its nonempty branch.

background_notes.justification: A real set lying in a ball of radius R about a lies in [a-R,a+R]. Conversely a set contained between real bounds p,q has distances from p bounded by max(q-p,0). The usual real order is conditionally complete. These facts identify the order and metric boundedness structures used in the stated application.

background_notes.fact: For arbitrary finite real endpoints a,b the interval [a,b] is closed, hence Borel measurable, also when empty. The empty set and finite intersections of such sets are Borel measurable.

grounds.reason: J_i is either empty or a closed real interval; I=[0,1].
D008 defines I.
D011 fixes the Borel measurable structure on R.

background_notes.justification: The complement of [a,b] is the union of the open rays (-infinity,a) and (b,infinity). Closed sets are complements of open sets and belong to the Borel sigma algebra, which is closed under finite intersections.

background_notes.fact: For u>0, the map d -> d^u is increasing on extended nonnegative reals. For finite r>=0, (ofReal(r))^u=ofReal(r^u); also (ofReal(r^u))*ofReal(r)=ofReal(r^(u+1)).

grounds.reason: F001 gives finite 0<=rho_i<=delta and the projection diameter bounds.
L1 gives s>0, hence s+1>0.
D018 supplies the standard power conventions.

background_notes.justification: On positive finite bases, monotonicity follows from increasing log and exp and multiplication by u>0. The identity r^u*r=r^(u+1) follows by adding exponents in exp(u log r). At r=0 both positive powers vanish, and the extended endpoints follow from 0^u=0 and infinity^u=infinity. Embedding finite nonnegative reals preserves products and the defined powers. These facts justify both the slice-cost comparison here and the termwise power identity in S005.

background_notes.fact: For any measurable set B in a measurable space and fixed k in [0,infinity], the function k1_B with values in [0,infinity] is measurable, including k=infinity. A measurable function is almost-everywhere measurable for every measure.

grounds.reason: F003 supplies measurability of I and every J_i intersect I.
h and g_i are exactly constant indicators on those sets.
D012 defines an indicator by its values, including an infinite constant.

background_notes.justification: The inverse image of a Borel set under k1_B is one of the empty set, B, its complement, or the entire space, depending on membership of 0 and k. All are measurable. Almost-everywhere measurability then holds using the function itself as the measurable representative, with no exceptional set.

background_notes.fact: Multiplication by a fixed nonnegative extended scalar preserves inequalities (with 0*infinity=0). For sequences a_i<=b_i in [0,infinity], sum_i a_i<=sum_i b_i, without finiteness assumptions.

grounds.reason: F003 bounds volume(J_i) by ofReal(rho_i).
The displayed chain multiplies measure inequalities by nonnegative ofReal(rho_i^s) and then sums.
D011 supplies measure monotonicity on J_i intersect I subset J_i.

background_notes.justification: For finite nonnegative scalars multiplication is order preserving; the zero and infinity cases satisfy the same inequality directly under the stated conventions. Compare each finite partial sum termwise, then take the supremum over finite index sets, which defines the nonnegative extended sum.

background_notes.fact: In [0,infinity], if c<=k for every member k of a family K, then c<=inf K, including K empty with inf K=infinity. If f(delta)<=g(delta) for every delta>0, then sup_{delta>0} f(delta)<=sup_{delta>0} g(delta), including infinite suprema.

grounds.reason: F005 makes C_s(delta,A) a lower bound for every admissible product-cover cost.
N101 identifies these infima with the positive-exponent contents and identifies the scale suprema with H.
The scale inequality has been proved for arbitrary positive delta and s+1 is positive.

background_notes.justification: An infimum is the greatest lower bound, so every lower bound is below it; for an empty family this says only c<=infinity. Each f(delta) is below the supremum of g, making that supremum an upper bound for all f(delta); the least-upper-bound property yields the stated supremum inequality. No interchange of infimum, supremum or integral is involved.
